records.title: Discussion shared in Scotland Against Spin, 26 September 2026
records.bodyText:
The UK government has paid almost twice as much to turn off windfarms in Scotland as it plans to spend on developing small modular nuclear reactors by the end of this decade, industry leaders have said.
The Nuclear Industry Association said ministers plan to invest £2.8 billion in the technology, compared with£5.1bn in so called constraint payments that have been made since 2021.
Some £1.04bn was forked out in constraint payments this year up until the end of August. This is up from £648 min the same period last year.
The UK Government wants to open small modular reactors in Scotland, potentially at former nuclear sites such as Torness, Hunterston, and Dounreay. All of these sites already have grid transmission connections. But this has been blocked by the Scottish government which holds planning powers.
SCOTSMAN.COM 'UK spends twice as much switching off windfarms as it does on nuclear reactors'

records.title: Discussion shared in Communities B4 Power Companies, 25 September 2026
records.bodyText:
I get bored of the relentless drone by many about how Scotland is producing energy for England, which of course it does, but that favour flows north too. And east, and west.
It is called a 'national grid'.
The evidence shows England having a greater installed capacity and producing more of everything renewable. I came across this site, but it is from 2024. My argument now, and always has been, is WHO will Scotland export all this surplus energy to if their nearest neighbour is producing twice as much already, and building nuclear?
If anyone has more up to date stats, please advise, including actual TWh installed capacity and output for 2025-6. Installed capacity does not mean actual production, especially as so much production in Scotland is curtailed.
Thanks!
https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/media/68da6dc6ef1c2f72bc1e4b72/Regional_renewable_electricity_in_2024.pdf

records.title: Discussion shared in Scotland Against Spin, 26 September 2026
records.bodyText:
Herald letters
UKRAINE fired more than 1,000 drones at Russia, and Russia retaliated using drones to attack Ukraine's southern city of Zaporizhzhia.
This made me think about the greenhouse gases created by wars all around the world. Why have politicians and those of a green disposition never told us the volume of emissions created by the Russian war against Ukraine, and the emissions that will be created in rebuilding the shattered infrastructure?
Then, of course, there is mother nature, with her volcanoes, earthquakes, tsunamis, hurricanes and more. All emitting greenhouse gases which puny mankind can never control. No figure has been put on that either. What about music and sporting events? Do politicians really believe people will believe that buying an EV and a heat pump, and cycling to work and eating less meat, will save the planet?
Meanwhile, most of the rest of the world is still harvesting and using fossil fuels to drive their economies.
Clark Cross, Linlithgow.

records.title: Discussion shared in Scotland Against Spin, 25 September 2026
records.bodyText:
The Labour government has made “no detailed assessment” of how much China owns of a “key part of the UK'S energy system” – despite blocking a major Chinese wind turbine project for national security reasons.
It comes after ministers blocked the £1.5 billion Ming Yang turbine factory in the Highlands earlier this year because of national security concerns about the firm.
The SNP said the recent “revelation” showed the Ming Yang decision was “entirely political”.
SNP Energy spokesperson Graham Leadbitter questioned why Chinese firms were allowed to invest in battery storage, but not allowed to open a factory in the Highlands.
SCOTSMAN.COM UK government has 'no detailed assessment' of Chinese battery storage ownership
